messages.author: 80b61c27b565cdf3
messages.subject: reparametrizing a half-cauchy
parts:
Quick sanity check; I want to replace the uniform prior on a variance parameter with a half cauchy, as suggested in the manual. I'm using:

real<lower=0> sigma; 
...
sigma ~ cauchy(0, scale) //scale is an input to the program

The manual also suggests I should reparametrize the cauchy to avoid sampling problems:

real <lower=-pi()/2, upper=pi()/2> sigma_unif;
...
real sigma;
sigma <- 0 + scale * tan(sigma_unif);
....
sigma_unif ~ uniform(-pi()/2, pi()/2)) //not necessary

Of course this is the parametrization for a full, not half, cauchy, which is inappropriate for a scale parameter. Is the solution to set the lower limit of sigma_unif to 0 instead of pi/2? That produces the desire half cauchy right?

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] reparametrizing a half-cauchy
parts:
Hi, just a quick comment which is that you could use something like a t_4 which could behave more reasonably.
(My bad for suggesting the Cauchy in the first place, I guess!)
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] reparametrizing a half-cauchy
parts:
You shouldn't need to reparameterize in this case, but
yes, that'd be the right way to do it (though don't use
(0 + x) as it's just wasted arithmetic).

As a general piece of advice, get things working first,
then optimize if they aren't fast enough.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: reparametrizing a half-cauchy

Thanks for the replies! 

I guess I can see the point in not wanting the particularly long tail, which actually makes sense given that I'm using logistic regression, and large variance won't make a difference inside the inv logit. That being said, in my application there will be usually be a large number of groups (30-100) which probably means there's lower risk for the scale to overfit with large values. 

That being said, I'll probably switch to a half normal or half-t. As a follow-up, is there a non-aesthetic reason why I might prefer one of those two over the other?

Thanks again!
Ted

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] reparametrizing a half-cauchy
parts:
Such reparameterizations aren’t so much for increased speed but rather
improved robustness.  Cauchy’s are difficult to sample because the heavy
tails take forever to explore, but an auxiliary parameterization yields much
nicer tails at the expense of the extra parameters.  Whether the expense
is worth it or not depends on how much time you end up spending in the
tails — if you have lots of data then the posterior will have nice tails and
it won’t matter, but if you have sparse data then it could make a significant
difference.
